record.paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
record.original_question: What is the minimum possible number of vertices in a planar hypohamiltonian graph, where planar means drawable in the plane without edge crossings? If N is that minimum, does there exist a planar hypohamiltonian graph on every n at least N, or are some orders missing?

evidence.quote: There also exist infinitely many planar hypohamiltonian graphs. (A planar graph is one that can be drawn in the plane without any edges crossing.)

Although we know that planar hypohamiltonian graphs exist we don’t know how small (in terms of vertices) they can be. Suppose the smallest planar hypohamiltonian graph had N vertices. Does there exist a planar hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices for all n > N or are there "gaps" ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph G is called hypohamiltonian if G itself has no Hamiltonian cycle, but for every vertex v of G, the graph G − v obtained by deleting v (and all incident edges) does have a Hamiltonian cycle. A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane with no two edges crossing.

(a) Determine the minimum number N of vertices of a planar hypohamiltonian graph; that is, find the smallest integer N such that there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph on N vertices.

(b) Let N be the value from part (a). Decide whether, for every integer n ≥ N, there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph on exactly n vertices, or whether there are "gaps" — values n ≥ N for which no planar hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact minimum order of a planar hypohamiltonian graph is still unknown. The smallest known planar hypohamiltonian graphs have 34 vertices (Tsai, 2024/2025), improving the prior bound of 40 (Jooyandeh, McKay, Östergård, Pettersson, Zamfirescu, 2017). The best known lower bound is around 23 vertices. Existence on orders 35, 36, 39 remains open, while planar hypohamiltonian graphs are known on 34, 37, 38, 40, and all sufficiently large orders. Hence the question of the minimum and the gap structure is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Small planar hypohamiltonian graphs (arXiv:2403.18384)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the smallest known planar hypohamiltonian graph from 40 to 34 vertices; existence on 35, 36, 39 vertices remains open; lower bound 23.
status_evidence.claim: Problem of minimum is still open; current best upper bound 34, lower bound 23.

status_evidence.title: Planar Hypohamiltonian Graphs on 40 Vertices (arXiv:1302.2698)
status_evidence.snippet: Jooyandeh, McKay, Östergård, Pettersson, Zamfirescu construct planar hypohamiltonian graphs on 40 vertices, previously the smallest known.
status_evidence.claim: Historic best upper bound was 40 vertices.

status_evidence.title: Hypohamiltonian graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses known constructions and orders for planar hypohamiltonian graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existence on every sufficiently large order is known but exact minimum and gaps are not fully determined.
